task.title: Links
task.shortdesc: A link points from an element to another part of the document or to an external address. XML has no standard names for links, so you use the CSSMedia property -cssmedia-link to tell CSSMedia which elements are links and where they go. The link reference lists the property, the function and the pseudo-classes used for links.

context.p: The element and attribute names in the examples, such as xref and target, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.

info.p: The -cssmedia-link property sets the destination of an element. It is a CSSMedia extension, so its name has the prefix -cssmedia-. Its value is none, which is the initial value and means that the element is not a link, or one or more of these:
CSSMedia joins the values in order, without spaces, to make the destination. The property is not inherited, so set it on each element that is a link. Use none to remove a link.
This XML has an xref element with a target attribute:
Use attr() to take the destination from the attribute:
The text of the element is the text of the link, and the attribute is its destination. If the attribute is missing, attr() gives an empty string, unless you give a fallback.
To link to a place in the same document, add # before the ID:
The link goes to #details, the element of the document with the ID details.
To link to an external address, write the address as a string:

A relative string, such as "chapter-2.xml#installation", is resolved against the address of the XML document. A url() value is resolved against the address of the stylesheet. Use a string when the address is relative to the XML document.
Setting -cssmedia-link does not change how a link looks. Use :any-link to select the elements that have a destination, and set the properties that you want:
:link selects the same elements, because a PDF has no visited links. :visited never matches.
:local-link selects the links that point to the same document. CSSMedia ignores the fragment when it compares the addresses, so a link to #details is a local link.

Add a number to compare part of the address: :local-link(0) selects the links with the same origin, which is the scheme, the host and the port. :local-link(1) also compares the first segment of the path, :local-link(2) the first two, and so on. Combine it with :not() to select the links to other origins:

step.cmd: Show a counter of the destination

info.p: -cssmedia-link-counter() gives the value of a counter at the destination of the link of an element. Use it in the content property, for example to show the number of the footnote that a link points to:

The element links to the element with the ID note-1 and shows the value of the footnote counter of that element. An optional second argument sets the counter style, as in -cssmedia-link-counter(footnote, lower-alpha).
